key_insight: A DIO/ODI-informed authorization boundary separates evidence an entity-resolution agent can reason with from evidence permitted to authorize persistent identity-changing mutations.
engineering_relevance: The design specifies commit-time controls for agentic entity resolution so plausible identity hypotheses alone cannot authorize graph changes.
method: Map selected identity-reconstruction failure distinctions to domain-governed, identity-preserving constraints.
Promote evidence separately for each claim; UNVERIFIED admission grants no authorization eligibility.
Use a two-phase supervisor to require proposition coverage, conflict resolution, authorized scope, and valid state and policy versions before commit.
evidence_signal: The paper proposes evaluation against generic authorization and conventional identifier rules but reports no implementation or empirical validation.
watch_item: Protection depends on adequate domain policy, evidence promotion, and enforcement; it does not prevent erroneous hypotheses or hypothesis-conditioned retrieval.
paper_title: Constraining the Commit Boundary: A DIO/ODI-Informed Authorization Guardrail for Agentic Entity Resolution
